verdict.rationale: Runpod's own docs describe Serverless Flex workers that "Scale to zero when idle" for variable workloads, billed per second only while a worker runs. Developers can deploy their own code to Serverless via Flash projects with GPU workers, and manage endpoints from the CLI. missing for 10: detailed documentation of autoscaling behavior (scale-up triggers, max worker limits) in the evidence, independent or hands-on corroboration of serverless scaling.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy code to autoscaling serverless GPU workers that scale to zero, instead of managing always-on instances

citations.quote: Flex workers | Scale to zero when idle | Standard per-second rate | Variable workloads, cost optimization
Serverless offers pay-per-second pricing with no upfront costs. You're billed from when a worker starts until it fully stops, rounded up to the nearest second.
you can ask your agent to create Pods, deploy Serverless endpoints, transfer files, or deploy your own code with Flash, all in natural language
Create a new Flash project with a ready-to-use template structure including a FastAPI server, example GPU and CPU workers, and configuration files.
